## Failed Tests — Detail

### ❌ Enter Loadings (ACB-3599) › AC07: Per Mille loading > $20.00 → maximum-per-mille error

**Acceptance Criteria (from user story):**

> AC07: When I enter a per mille loading greater than 20.00, Then error "The maximum per mille loading is $20.00".
> 
> Steps to reproduce:
> 1. New quote, price Life $200k, open Loadings. 2. In an enabled Per Mille field (Life), enter 20.01. 3. Blur/OK.
> 
> Expected: "The maximum per mille loading is $20.00".

**What was compared:**

| Check | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Per mille > $20 raises the maximum-per-mille error | The maximum per mille loading is $20.00 |   |

**Assertion failure:**

```
Error: AC07. Got:  

expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

Expected: true
```

![Enter Loadings (ACB-3599) › AC07: Per Mille loading > $20.00 → maximum-per-mille error](data:image/png;base64,)

## Skipped / Blocked Tests — Detail

### ⏭️ Enter Loadings (ACB-3599) › AC04/AC05/AC08: OK saves loadings + "Loadings have been applied" message + premium reflects loadings (per life)

**Acceptance Criteria (from user story):**

> AC04: OK saves + redirects to Quote + premium reflects updated loadings + "Loadings have been applied" under Total Yearly Premium. AC05: the down-arrow opens the Underwriting Guide in a new window. AC08: "Loadings have been applied" per life it was applied to.

**Why skipped:**

> Deferred: AC04/AC08 assert the premium CHANGES by the loading and the "Loadings have been applied" confirmation after OK — the premium delta is a pricing-engine value (not hand-verifiable), and reliably reading the post-OK confirmation needs the exact OK-button selector + a stable post-apply signal (the probe found "Cancel" but not a plain "OK" — the apply control needs pinning down). AC05 opens an EXTERNAL Underwriting Guide URL in a new window (leaves the app). Encode in a focused follow-up: pin the OK/apply control, assert the "Loadings have been applied" text (behavioural, not the $ value), and capture the window.open target for AC05.
